ZOOEPHORIC: Bearing or supporting the figure of an animal; as, a zoöphoric column.

Note: It is the rhizome of different species of Curcuma, esp. C. zedoaria, and comes in short, firm pieces, externally of a wrinkled gray, ash-colored appearance, but within of a brownish red colo...
ZOOEDENDRIUM: The branched, and often treelike, support of the colonies of certain Infusoria.
ZAPHRENTIS: An extinct genus of cyathophylloid corals common in the Paleozoic formations. It is cup-shaped with numerous septa, and with a deep pit in one side of the cup.
ZYMOGENE: One of a physiological group of globular bacteria which produces fermentations of diverse nature; -- distinguished from pathogene.
ZEPHYR: The west wind; poetically, any soft, gentle breeze. "Soft the zephyr blows." Gray. As gentle As zephyrs blowing below the violet. Shak. Zephyr cloth, a thin kind of cassimere made in Belgium; also, a waterproof fabric of wool. -- Zephyr shawl, a kind of thin, light, embroidered shawl made of worsted and cotton. -- Zephyr yarn, or worsted, a fine...
ZOOELOGIST: One who is well versed in zoölogy.
ZOPILOTE: The urubu, or American black vulture.
ZIEGA: Curd produced from milk by adding acetic acid, after rennet has ceased to cause coagulation. Brande & C.
ZOOEPHYTOLOGICAL: Of or pertaining to zoöphytology; as, zoöphytological observations.
ZEA: A genus of large grasses of which the Indian corn (Zea Mays) is the only species known. Its origin is not yet ascertained. See Maize.
ZOOELOGICAL: Of or pertaining to zoölogy, or the science of animals.
ZILLA: A low, thorny, suffrutescent, crucifeous plant (Zilla myagroides) found in the deserts of Egypt. Its leaves are boiled in water, and eaten, by the Arabs.
ZEBU: A bovine mammal (Ros Indicus) extensively domesticated in India, China, the East Indies, and East Africa. It usually has short horns, large pendulous ears, slender legs, a large dewlap, and a large, prominent hump over the shoulders; but these characters vary in different domestic breeds, which range in size from that of the common ox to that of...
ZEPPELIN: A dirigible balloon of the rigid type, consisting of a cylindrical trussed and covered frame supported by internal gas cells, and provided with means of propulsion and control. It was first successfully used by Ferdinand Count von Zeppelin.
ZATI: A species of macaque (Macacus pileatus) native of India and Ceylon. It has a crown of long erect hair, and tuft of radiating hairs on the back of the head. Called also capped macaque.
ZUNYITE: A fluosilicate of alumina occurring in tetrahedral crystals at the Zuñi mine in Colorado.
ZOOEPRAXISCOPE: An instrument similar to, or the same as, the, the phenakistoscope, by means of which pictures projected upon a screen are made to exhibit the natural movements of animals, and the like.
ZOO-: A combining form from Gr. zwo^,n an animal, as in zoögenic, zoölogy, etc.
ZOOMELANIN: A pigment giving the black color to the feathers of many birds.
ZOOPHAGAN: A animal that feeds on animal food.
ZOOETOMIST: One who dissects animals, or is skilled in zoötomy.
ZANTE CURRANT: A kind of seedless grape or raisin; -- so called from Zante, one of the Ionian Islands.
ZOOEN: (a) An animal which is the sole product of a single egg; -- opposed to zooid. H. Spencer. (b) Any one of the perfectly developed individuals of a compound animal.
ZOOPHOROUS: The part between the architrave and cornice; the frieze; -- so called from the figures of animals carved upon it.
ZIZANIA: A genus of grasses including Indian rice. See Indian rice, under Rice.
ZOSTERA: A genus of plants of the Naiadaceæ, or Pondweed family. Zostera marina is commonly known as sea wrack, and eelgrass.
ZAMOUSE: A West African buffalo (Bubalus brachyceros) having short horns depressed at the base, and large ears fringed internally with three rows of long hairs. It is destitute of a dewlap. Called also short- horned buffalo, and bush cow.
ZOOETOMY: The dissection or the anatomy of animals; -- distinguished from androtomy.
ZOOLOGIST: One who is well versed in zoölogy.
ZYMOTIC: 1. Of, pertaining to, or caused by, fermentation. 2. (Med.) Designating, or pertaining to, a certain class of diseases. See Zymotic disease, below. Zymotic disease (Med.), any epidemic, endemic, contagious, or sporadic affection which is produced by some morbific principle or organism acting on the system like a ferment.
ZOANTHROPY: A kind of monomania in which the patient believes himself transformed into one of the lower animals.
ZOANTHUS: A genus of Actinaria, including numerous species, found mostly in tropical seas. The zooids or polyps resemble small, elongated actinias united together at their bases by fleshy stolons, and thus forming extensive groups. The tentacles are small and bright colored.
ZOANTHODEME: The zooids of a compound anthozoan, collectively.
ZEALOTRY: The character and behavior of a zealot; excess of zeal; fanatical devotion to a cause. Enthusiasm, visionariness, seems the tendency of the German; zeal, zealotry, of the English; fanaticism, of the French. Coleridge.
ZOOPHAGOUS: Feeding on animals. Note: This is a more general term than either sarcophagous or carnivorous.
ZYMOGENIC: (a) Pertaining to, or formed by, a zymogene. (b) Capable of producing a definite zymogen or ferment. Zymogenic organism (Biol.), a microörganism, such as the yeast plant of the Bacterium lactis, which sets up certain fermentative processes by which definite chemical products are formed; -- distinguished from a pathogenic organism. Cf. Micrococcus.
ZAREBA: An improvised stockade; especially, one made of thorn bushes, etc. [Written also zareeba, and zeriba.] [Egypt] "Ah," he moralizes, "what wonderful instinct on the part of this little creature to surround itself with a zareba like the troops after Osman Digma." R. Jefferies.
ZEUGLODON: A genus of extinct Eocene whales, remains of which have been found in the Gulf States. The species had very long and slender bodies and broad serrated teeth. See Phocodontia.
ZONED: 1. Wearing a zone, or girdle. Pope. 2. Having zones, or concentric bands; striped. 3. (Bot.) Zonate.
ZOOSPORANGIUM: A spore, or conceptacle containing zoöspores.
ZARATHUSTRIC: Of or pertaining to Zarathustra, or Zoroaster; Zoroastrian. Tylor.
ZYMOME: A glutinous substance, insoluble in alcohol, resembling legumin; -- now called vegetable fibrin, vegetable albumin, or gluten casein.
ZOONITE: (a) One of the segments of the body of an articulate animal. (b) One of the theoretic transverse divisions of any segmented animal.
ZACHUN: An oil pressed by the Arabs from the fruit of a small thorny tree (Balanites Ægyptiaca), and sold to piligrims for a healing ointment. J. Smith (Dict. Econ. Plants).
ZOOPRAXISCOPE: An instrument similar to, or the same as, the, the phenakistoscope, by means of which pictures projected upon a screen are made to exhibit the natural movements of animals, and the like.
ZOOECHLORELLA: One of the small green granulelike bodies found in the interior of certain stentors, hydras, and other invertebrates.
ZAMINDARY: The jurisdiction of a zamindar; the land possessed by a zamindar. [Written also zemindary, zemindari.]
ZOOECYTIUM: The common support, often branched, of certain species of social Infusoria.
ZYMOLOGIST: One who is skilled in zymology, or in the fermentation of liquors.
ZINCIFICATION: The act or process of applying zinc; the condition of being zincified, or covered with zinc; galvanization.
ZEST: 1. A piece of orange or lemon peel, or the aromatic oil which may be squeezed from such peel, used to give flavor to liquor, etc. 2. Hence, something that gives or enhances a pleasant taste, or the taste itself; an appetizer; also, keen enjoyment; relish; gusto. ZOOGONY: The doctrine of the formation of living beings.
ZOOEGRAPHICAL: Of or pertaining to the description of animals.
ZOEA: A peculiar larval stage of certain decapod Crustacea, especially of crabs and certain Anomura. [Written also zoæa.] Note: In this stage the anterior part of the body is relatively large, and usually bears three or four long spines. ZIGZAGGERY: The quality or state of being zigzag; crookedness. [R.] The . . . zigzaggery of my father's approaches. Sterne.
ZYGODACTYLOUS: Yoke-footed; having the toes disposed in pairs; -- applied to birds which have two toes before and two behind, as the parrot, cuckoo, woodpecker, etc.
ZYMOLYSIS: The action of enzymes; also, the changes produced by such action. --Zy`mo*lyt"ic (#), a.
ZUNIS: A tribe of Pueblo Indians occupying a village in New Mexico, on the Zuni River.
ZOOEPHAGAN: A animal that feeds on animal food.
ZOOCYTIUM: The common support, often branched, of certain species of social Infusoria.
ZIRCONIA: The oxide of zirconium, obtained as a white powder, and possessing both acid and basic properties. On account of its infusibility, and brilliant luminosity when incandescent, it is used as an ingredient of sticks for the Drummomd light.
ZOOESPORE: 1. (Bot.) A spore provided with one or more slender cilia, by the vibration of which it swims in the water. Zoöspores are produced by many green, and by some olive-brown, algæ. In certain species they are divided into the larger macrozoöspores and the smaller microzoöspores. Called also sporozoid, and swarmspore. 2. (Zoöl.) See Swarmspore.
ZIETRISIKITE: A mineral wax, vert similar to ozocerite. It is found at Zietrisika, Moldavia, whence its name.
ZOONIC: Of or pertaining to animals; obtained from animal substances.
ZINCING: The act or process of applying zinc; galvanization.
ZOISM: 1. Reverence for animal life or belief in animal powers and influences, as among savages. 2. (Biol.) A doctrine, now discarded, that the phenomena of life are due to a peculiar vital principle; the theory of vital force.
ZALAMBDODONT: Of or pertaining to a tribe (Zalambdodonta) of Insectivora in which the molar teeth have but one V-shaped ridge. One of the Zalambdodonta. The tenrec, solenodon, and golden moles are examples.
ZONURE: Any one of several of South African lizards of the genus Zonura, common in rocky situations.
ZINCO-: A combining form from zinc; in chemistry, designating zinc as an element of certain double compounds. Also used adjectively.
ZOODENDRIUM: The branched, and often treelike, support of the colonies of certain Infusoria.
ZOOIDAL: Of or pertaining to a zooid; as, a zooidal form.
ZAMINDARI: The jurisdiction of a zamindar; the land possessed by a zamindar. [Written also zemindary, zemindari.]
ZOOEGEOGRAPHY: The study or description of the geographical distribution of animals.
ZOANTHARIAN: Of or pertaining to the Zoantharia. -- n. One of the Anthozoa.
ZOOESPORANGIUM: A spore, or conceptacle containing zoöspores.
ZARNICH: Native sulphide of arsenic, including sandarach, or realgar, and orpiment.
ZOOTOMIST: One who dissects animals, or is skilled in zoötomy.
ZEBRAWOOD: (a) A kind of cabinet wood having beautiful black, brown, and whitish stripes, the timber of a tropical American tree (Connarus Guianensis). (b) The wood of a small West Indian myrtaceous tree (Eugenia fragrans). (c) The wood of an East Indian tree of the genus Guettarda.
ZYGOMA: (a) The jugal, malar, or cheek bone. (b) The zygomatic process of the temporal bone. (c) The whole zygomatic arch.
ZOOETROPHIC: Of or pertaining to the nourishment of animals.
ZINCOGRAPHY: The art or process of engraving or etching on zinc, in which the design is left in relief in the style of a wood cut, the rest of the ground being eaten away by acid.
ZOOEERYTHRINE: A peculiar organic red coloring matter found in the feathers of various birds.
ZARF: A metallic cuplike stand used for holding a finjan.
ZINCO-POLAR: Electrically polarized like the surface of the zinc presented to the acid in a battery, which has zincous affinity. [Obs.]
ZOOEGRAPHIC: Of or pertaining to the description of animals.
ZOBO: A kind of domestic cattle reared in Asia for its flesh and milk. It is supposed to be a hybrid between the zebu and the yak.
ZONULAR: Of or pertaining to a zone; zone-shaped. "The zonular type of a placenta." Dana.
ZOHAR: A Jewish cabalistic book attributed by tradition to Rabbi Simon ben Yochi, who lived about the end of the 1st century, a. d. Modern critics believe it to be a compilation of the 13th century. Encyc. Brit.
ZAERTHE: Same as Zärthe. A European bream (Abramis vimba). [Written also zaerthe.]
ZOLAESQUE: In the style of Zola (see Zolaism).
ZOUNDS: An exclamation formerly used as an oath, and an expression of anger or wonder.
ZINCODE: The positive electrode of an electrolytic cell; anode. [R.] Miller.
ZOOGENIC: Of or pertaining to zoögeny, animal production.
ZEHNER: An Austrian silver coin equal to ten kreutzers, or about five cents.
ZOIC: Of or pertaining to animals, or animal life.
ZYGODACTYLAE: The zygodactylous birds. In a restricted sense applied to a division of birds which includes the barbets, toucans, honey guides, and other related birds.
ZOOEPHYTA: An extensive artificial and heterogeneous group of animals, formerly adopted by many zoölogists. It included the coelenterates, echinoderms, sponges, Bryozoa, Protozoa, etc. Note: Sometimes the name is restricted to the Coelentera, or to the Anthozoa.
ZYGOPHYTE: Any plant of a proposed class or grand division (Zygophytes, Zygophyta, or Zygosporeæ), in which reproduction consists in the union of two similar cells. Cf. Oöphyte.
ZIBET: A carnivorous mammal (Viverra zibetha) closely allied to the civet, from which it differs in having the spots on the body less distinct, the throat whiter, and the black rings on the tail more numerous. ZIRCO-: A combining form (also used adjectively) designating zirconium as an element of certain double compounds; zircono-; as in zircofluoric acid, sodium zircofluoride.
ZEOLITE: A term now used to designate any one of a family of minerals, hydrous silicates of alumina, with lime, soda, potash, or rarely baryta. Here are included natrolite, stilbite, analcime, chabazite, thomsonite, heulandite, and others. These species occur of secondary origin in the cavities of amygdaloid, basalt, and lava, also, less frequently, in g...
ZEBUB: A large noxious fly of Abyssinia, which like the tsetse fly, is destructive to cattle.
ZOOPHYTE: (a) Any one of numerous species of invertebrate animals which more or less resemble plants in appearance, or mode of growth, as the corals, gorgonians, sea anemones, hydroids, bryozoans, sponges, etc., especially any of those that form compound colonies having a branched or treelike form, as many corals and hydroids. (b) Any one of the Zoöphyta.
ZOOEGRAPHY: A description of animals, their forms and habits.
ZEOLITIC: Of or pertaining to a zeolite; consisting of, or resembling, a zeolite.
ZOOEPHOROUS: The part between the architrave and cornice; the frieze; -- so called from the figures of animals carved upon it.
ZOOECIUM: One of the cells or tubes which inclose the feeling zooids of Bryozoa. See Illust. of Sea Moss.
ZEALOTICAL: Like, or suitable to, a zealot; ardently zealous. [R.] Strype.
ZOOPHYTOLOGICAL: Of or pertaining to zoöphytology; as, zoöphytological observations.
ZOOGRAPHY: A description of animals, their forms and habits.
ZOOELOGICALLY: In a zoölogical manner; according to the principles of zoölogy.
ZITHER: An instrument of music used in Austria and Germany. It has from thirty to forty wires strung across a shallow sounding-board, which lies horizontally on a table before the performer, who uses both hands in playing on it. Note: [Not to be confounded with the old lute-shaped cittern, or cithern.]
ZOOGLOEA: A colony or mass of bacteria imbedded in a viscous gelatinous substance. The zoögloea is characteristic of a transitory stage through which rapidly multiplying bacteria pass in the course of their evolution. Also used adjectively.
ZIKKURAT: A temple tower of the Babylonians or Assyrians, consisting of a lofty pyramidal structure, built in successive stages, with outside staircases, and a shrine at the top.
ZIMENT-WATER: A kind of water found in copper mines; water impregnated with copper.
ZINCIFY: To coat or impregnate with zinc.
ZOOERYTHRINE: A peculiar organic red coloring matter found in the feathers of various birds.
ZOOGEOGRAPHY: The study or description of the geographical distribution of animals.
ZYGOSPHENE: A median process on the front part of the neural arch of the vertebræ of most snakes and some lizards, which fits into a fossa, called the zygantrum, on the back part of the arch in front.
ZOOGENY: The doctrine of the formation of living beings.
ZOOID: Pertaining to, or resembling, an animal. 1. (Biol.) An organic body or cell having locomotion, as a spermatic cell or spermatozooid. 2. (Zoöl.) (a) An animal in one of its inferior stages of development, as one of the intermediate forms in alternate generation. (b) One of the individual animals in a composite group, as of Anthozoa, Hydroidea, an...
ZIF: The second month of the Jewish ecclesiastical year, corresponding to our May.
ZOOENIC: Of or pertaining to animals; obtained from animal substances.
ZWIEBACK: A kind of biscuit or rusk first baked in a loaf and afterwards cut and toasted.
ZOISITE: A grayish or whitish mineral occurring in orthorhombic, prismatic crystals, also in columnar masses. It is a silicate of alumina and lime, and is allied to epidote.
ZENANA: The part of a dwelling appropriated to women. [India]
ZOOLOGICALLY: In a zoölogical manner; according to the principles of zoölogy.
ZIONISM: Among the Jews, a theory, plan, or movement for colonizing their own race in Palestine, the land of Zion, or, if that is impracticable, elsewhere, either for religious or nationalizing purposes; -- called also Zion movement. --Zi"on*ist, n. -- Zi`on*is"tic (#), a.
ZYMOSIMETER: An instrument for ascertaining the degree of fermentation occasioned by the mixture of different liquids, and the degree of heat which they acquire in fermentation.
ZINCOGRAPH: A zinc plate prepared for printing by zincography; also, a print from such a plate.
